Later this fall, Apple will update the Mac Studio, which has remained unchanged since early 2025. Though it's only been about a year, the update is significant because the current top-of-the-line Mac Studio still uses the M3 chip, and Apple has never released an M4 Ultra variant. Here's a preview of the next-generation Mac Studio and what's ahead.

This Fall

The Mac Studio with M5 was originally expected to launch in mid-2026, but ongoing memory shortages have pushed the timeline back slightly. According to rumors, the new machine could debut as early as October.

This update will introduce Mac Studio models with M5 Max and M5 Ultra chips, with the M5 Ultra potentially offering up to 768GB of memory. However, due to supply chain constraints, whether Apple can actually deliver configurations with that much memory remains unknown.

The M5 Ultra will feature up to a 36-core CPU and 80-core GPU, delivering significant performance gains over the current M3 Ultra model.

The Mac Studio M4 Max and M3 Ultra versions were originally priced at $1,999 and $3,999 respectively, but after price increases, they have been adjusted to $2,499 and $5,299 — the new M5-powered models could be priced even higher.

2028

In 2028, Apple will update the Mac Studio again with M7 Max and M7 Ultra chips, and the changes will be even more substantial.

The M7 series chips are rumored to bring major leaps in AI performance, potentially making the M7 Ultra a true monster for running on-device large language models (LLMs).

The new machine may also see changes to its exterior design, though specific details have yet to be finalized.

Beyond the performance gains of the M7 series, the Mac Studio with M7 Ultra has two notable upgrades: a newly designed heatsink for more sustained performance, and the possibility of supporting up to 1.5TB of memory. Again, actual availability remains a variable, but Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman reports that Apple is developing the M7 Ultra to support 1.5TB of unified memory.

Interestingly, the new machine could finally catch up to the 2019 Mac Pro — which supported up to 1.5TB of RAM, the most ever in a Mac. Based on Apple's current memory pricing, upgrading from 128GB to 1.5TB of memory could cost around $35,000 (not including the required CPU upgrade costs).
